what.text: This page follows people displaced inside Brazil, as counted by IDMC.
At the end of 2025, IDMC counted 19043 people living in internal displacement because of conflict and violence.
Refugees from Brazil live mostly in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for Brazil; IDMC counts displacement from conflict and violence.
Droughts, erosion, extreme temperatures, floods, mass movements, storms and wildfires are the disasters recorded for Brazil in IDMC's data.

when.text: IDMC's figures fell from 20689 in 2021 to 5582 in 2022 and then rose again.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2021 and 2023 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say where displaced people are living or which routes they took.
IDMC also counts new displacements from disasters in each year, which count movements, not people, so someone forced to move twice is counted twice.
